description: Merhaba! Ben Zümra Payas. Bilim, uzay ve teknolojiye ilgi duyan; Python, Arduino ve 3D tasarım alanlarında kendini geliştiren bir lise öğrencisiyim. NASA Space Apps Challenge deneyimimle uzay ve mühendislik alanındaki ilgimi pekiştirdim. Ekibimizde yaratıcı fikirler geliştirmeyi, birlikte öğrenmeyi ve problemlere yenilikçi çözümler üretmeyi hedefliyoruz. Yazılım, astronomi, mühendislik ve tasarıma ilgi duyan, araştırmayı ve takım çalışmasını seven ekip arkadaşları arıyoruz!
summary:
Arthemis is an interactive space simulation that takes the player from Earth to the Moon, allowing them to directly manage an astronaut’s missions. Players configure their rocket, adjust orbital maneuvers, and select from various tasks on the Moon—such as collecting samples, operating a greenhouse, or conducting seismic research. The interface and mission content are in English.

The difficulty increases progressively through resource management and the consequences of errors: the astronaut’s supplies—such as energy and oxygen—are automatically replenished when they return to the spacecraft, while mistakes in orbital angles or thrust can jeopardize the entire mission. If delicate, expansive panels break during launch, the mission restarts with 150 credits, accompanied by a report explaining the cause of the failure. If greenhouse conditions are not maintained, the plants will die; in such cases, the greenhouse stages are reset, though seeds and credits are retained, and the astronaut is returned to the greenhouse entrance. Furthermore, limits on sample capacity and mission rewards encourage players to make deliberate, well-planned choices.
details: This project, developed within the Visual Studio Code environment, is an interactive, decision-based space mission simulation that spans the entire journey—from rocket launch and lunar landing to the rotation of the Earth. Upon reaching the Moon, the player is presented with a digital "Mission Tablet," where they can choose to undertake one of several objectives—such as collecting samples, establishing a greenhouse in the lunar regolith, or creating a seismological map—and work through the necessary sub-tasks. The most unique and creative aspect of the project is that the player's choices—grounded in actual scientific data (including solar winds, radiation shielding, light wavelengths for photosynthesis, background noise, and storage parameters)—lead directly to tangible, real-world consequences within the simulation. Designed with a modular code structure and robust error handling, this game aims to foster an interest in space sciences among children and young people, enhance their ability to think by establishing cause-and-effect relationships, and provide an engaging learning experience that makes the act of exploration feel deeply human.
